summary: Yellowstone ground cabin built in 1937 as a primary lookout; still standing, registered on NHLR in 2021 and kept as a fire lookout.

facts.design: 14x14 ground cabin with glass on four sides

staffing.status: intermittent per NHLR; last listed year 1993

access.note: Fire lookout in Yellowstone; a visitor account describes a 34-mile round trip on foot with permits required for overnight stays.

visit.trail_note: Reached on foot from a trailhead. One visitor account describes 34 miles round trip with permits required for overnight stays.

facts.agency: National Park Service, Yellowstone National Park

events.note: Erected by the CCC and finished by the park carpenter, per NHLR. 1937 newspapers announced it as a new primary lookout.
Staffed again from 1984 to 1988 and in 1993, per NHLR.
Date registered on the National Historic Lookout Register: March 1, 2021.

evidence.supports: 14x14 ground cabin erected in 1937 by the CCC
evidence.quote: Pelican Cone is a 14x14 ground cabin erected in 1937 by the CCC

evidence.supports: primary or secondary detection depending on source
evidence.quote: The lookout served either primary or secondary detection duty depending on the source.
Staffed from 1937 to 1974 and again from 1984 to 1988 and in 1993.

evidence.supports: used to watch fires, maintained as lookout
evidence.quote: Currently maintained as a fire lookout and periodically used to monitor fires in the Park.
Building #724, Yellowstone National Park, Park County, Wyoming.

evidence.supports: July 19, 1937 newspaper item: new primary lookout in east-central section
evidence.quote: In an effort to increase the protection a new primary lookout will be constructed during the summer at Pelican Cone in the east central section of the park.

evidence.supports: fourth primary lookout with four glass sides
evidence.quote: The building with its four glass sides will be the fourth primary lookout in the park.
At 34 miles round trip from the trail head
The lookout was not a tower, but was only a cabin perched on the bald mountain top.

evidence.supports: six visitors or fewer in a summer as described by staffer
evidence.quote: He said that in a given summer, he would expect to see half dozen visitors, or fewer.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 9,663 ft (2,945 m). firelookout.com and a visitor account give 9,650 ft. The story reports both and does not pick one.
NHLR says the lookout served primary or secondary detection depending on the source. The 1937 newspapers describe it as a primary lookout. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Built, staffing and registration rest on the NHLR page. The 1937 newspaper wording is quoted second-hand on the Forest Lookouts page; the newspapers themselves were not checked. Access and hike details come from one personal visitor account, which is undated, so treat them as indicative. No specific fires are named in the sources. The brief's access 'unknown' could become 'restricted' once the NPS status is confirmed. No photo URLs were added.
